items.description: Helpers come from the library chart dependency (charts.home), replacing the `charts/shared` symlinks, with no vendoring. `chart/Chart.yaml` pins `homelab-shared` exactly from `https://charts.home`. No template is a symlink, and no helper or built dependency is committed. The chart renders once the dependency is built.
items.rationale: chart/Chart.yaml declares an exact (non-range) dependency on homelab-shared 0.2.0 from https://charts.home, comment states it is deliberately exact (D17). chart/Chart.lock is committed with a digest; chart/charts/ is gitignored (never committed). No _helpers.tpl file exists anywhere under chart/templates (it is resolved from the dependency, not a symlink). The gate (tests/build-deps.sh + helm lint, part of `kc project lint`/`test`, GREEN per the r2 sweep) builds the dependency and renders both stages.

items.description: `deployment.timestamp` value changes; the key stays. On the controller pod template, the `deployment` annotation (the key `KUBECODER_DEPLOYMENT_ID`'s fieldRef reads) carries the controllerConfig checksum. The value is never empty, is identical across two renders of the same commit, and differs when controllerConfig changes. No rendered value derives from the render time.
items.rationale: controller-deployment.yaml:25-27 sets `$configChecksum := .Values.controllerConfig | toYaml | sha256sum` and stamps both `deployment` and `checksum/config` from it — a pure function of values, so two renders of one commit are byte-identical and it changes only when controllerConfig changes; sha256sum never returns empty. The KUBECODER_DEPLOYMENT_ID env var reads `metadata.annotations['deployment']` back via fieldRef (:95-98), the same key. The gate's render test asserts two renders >1s apart are identical (P3 done-record) and is GREEN.

items.description: The bot and MCP Deployments carry no deployment stamp. They roll only when their own pin or spec changes.
items.rationale: bot-deployment.yaml and mcp-deployment.yaml's pod template metadata carries only `labels`, no `annotations` block at all — no `deployment` or `checksum/config` stamp on either.

items.description: `global.environment` is declared in both `config/{stage}/values.yaml`, each with a comment saying it carries the *stage*. The dev and prd renders name ClusterRole `kubecoder-<stage>-nodes`, give its binding's subject the namespace `kubecoder-<stage>`, and claim `kubecoder-<stage>-zfs-pvc`.
items.rationale: Both config/dev/values.yaml:1-3 and config/prd/values.yaml:1-4 declare `global.environment` (dev / prd) with a comment naming it as the stage carrier. controller-clusterrole.yaml:5 and controller-clusterrolebinding.yaml:4-11 and zfs-pvc.yaml:5,14 all key off `.Values.global.environment` for the ClusterRole name, the binding's subject namespace, and the PVC/PV names.

items.description: The chart renders the stage's `Namespace` manifest (D25) with `sync-wave: "-1"` and `Prune=false`, replacing `module.namespace`. Nothing in KubeCoderDeploy's Terraform creates or manages a namespace.
items.rationale: chart/templates/namespace.yaml renders a Namespace named `.Release.Namespace` with annotations `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "-1"` and `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false`. terraform/ (providers.tf, storage.tf, webhook.tf, variables.tf) declares only homelab_zfs_dataset, kubernetes_persistent_volume_v1 and github_repository_webhook — no kubernetes_namespace resource anywhere.

items.description: The hook Job template is included from the library chart. Rendered with the four `hook.*` values the ApplicationSet passes, the chart yields the `tf-presync-` PreSync Job in `argocd-hooks`. Rendered without them, it fails.
items.rationale: chart/templates/tf-presync-hook.yaml is a one-line include of `homelab-shared.tf-presync-hook`. The library `required`-guards all four hook.* values (repo/revision/stage/namespace); the gate's helm lint and render-chart.py pass all four and are GREEN, and .kubecoder/project.yaml's lint stanza shows the render fails without them (the four --set are mandatory in every lint/test invocation).

items.description: AppProject: KubeCoder's ClusterRole and binding are whitelisted (cluster-scoped and tracked, so the cascade removes them on teardown). The `releases` whitelist already carries both, and the slice changes no AppProject. No stage render of KubeCoderDeploy's chart contains a cluster-scoped kind outside that whitelist.
items.rationale: ArgoCDDeploy's only change this slice (d2aa093) touches hook-namespace.yaml, config/prd/values.yaml and tests/render-chart.py — appproject.yaml is untouched, confirming the pre-existing whitelist (:40-47) stands unmodified. The KubeCoderDeploy chart renders one cluster-scoped ClusterRole + ClusterRoleBinding pair (kubecoder-<stage>-nodes), already on that whitelist.
evidence: ArgoCDDeploy d2aa093 diff --stat: hook-namespace.yaml, config/prd/values.yaml, tests/render-chart.py only

items.description: Terraform is rebuilt (D12 licence): the ZFS PV is all that remains, inlined with no module ceremony, and `config/{stage}/*.tfvars` carry the stage differences. For each stage, the dataset, quota, PV and claim it describes match what HelmCharts' `module.zfs` manages today, so slice 012's state move plans no change. The homelab provider block takes `zfs_pools` from the variable the hook's `TF_VAR_zfs_pools` fills (ruling F2). It is formatted and validates.
items.rationale: terraform/storage.tf declares homelab_zfs_dataset.env_storage (pool zpool5, prevent_destroy) and kubernetes_persistent_volume_v1.env_storage inline (Retain, claimRef, node_affinity to the pool's node) — no module block anywhere. providers.tf's `provider "homelab" { zfs_pools = var.zfs_pools }` matches HelmCharts' _providers/providers.tf precedent (ruling F2). config/{dev,prd}/terraform.tfvars carry zfs_dataset/zfs_quota/zfs_size/manage_webhook per stage, matching the live dataset/quota/size pairs recorded in the plan (20G/20Gi dev, 80G/80Gi prd). `kc project lint`/`test` (fmt -check, validate, mocked `terraform test` per stage) are GREEN.
evidence: sweeps/r2/KubeCoderDeploy_root_lint.log, KubeCoderDeploy_root_test.log — GREEN (fmt -check, validate, terraform test)

items.description: The deploy-repo webhook is a TF resource (D39), with `manage_webhook` true in exactly one stage's tfvars: `config/dev/`. The resource registers KubeCoderDeploy's push deliveries at `https://deploy-hooks.webathome.org/api/webhook`, signed with the shared webhook secret it reads from the hook environment.
items.rationale: terraform/webhook.tf's `github_repository_webhook.argocd` is gated on `count = var.manage_webhook ? 1 : 0`, posts push events to the relay URL over JSON with `secret = var.github_webhook_secret`. config/dev/terraform.tfvars sets `manage_webhook = true`; config/prd/terraform.tfvars sets it `false`, with a comment naming dev as the owner. variables.tf declares `github_webhook_secret` as sensitive, sourced from the hook's TF_VAR_github_webhook_secret (added by P1).

items.description: `argocd-hook-credentials` carries Argo's webhook shared secret, fetched from `eso/prd/argocd/prd/webhook` property `github_secret`, under the key KubeCoderDeploy's webhook Terraform reads. ArgoCDDeploy's render gate asserts the extended key set.
items.rationale: config/prd/values.yaml adds `TF_VAR_github_webhook_secret: {key: eso/prd/argocd/prd/webhook, property: github_secret}` under hooks.environment.leaves. tests/render-chart.py's HOOK_LEAVES gains the same key/leaf/property (exact-key-set assertion), and check_hook_environment() was extended to bind that value to what argocd-secret's webhook.github.secret reference resolves to, so the hook signs with the same value the relay/receivers verify. `kc project lint`/`test` are GREEN.

items.description: The `tf-presync` hook's cluster-wide ClusterRole no longer grants `namespaces`. `persistentvolumes` and `secrets` keep their full lifecycle, still with no wildcard. ArgoCDDeploy's render gate fails if a namespace grant returns.
items.rationale: hook-namespace.yaml's ClusterRole rule for core-group resources now lists only `secrets` (namespaces removed); the persistentvolumes rule is untouched, both still full LIFECYCLE verbs with no wildcard resource. tests/render-chart.py's HOOK_MANAGED is now (persistentvolumes, secrets), and a new HOOK_REFUSED = ("namespaces",) constant plus a check_hook_rbac() loop fails the gate if any ClusterRole rule names namespaces.

items.description: `audit-prd-orphans` becomes reconciler-aware. An entry Argo owns is not counted as a desired Helm release, so it is not reported missing, while its namespace and storage stay desired. It carries one guard: Argo's own bootstrap Helm release (`argocd-prd`) is not reported as an orphan to uninstall. HelmCharts' suite covers both.
items.rationale: desired_state() now reads `rel.get("reconciler", "jenkins")`; a non-jenkins entry goes into a new `owned_elsewhere` set instead of helm_releases, while its namespace/storage capture is unconditional (unaffected). cmd_diff() subtracts `desired["owned_elsewhere"]` from live Helm releases before the orphan diff and lists them apart with "never uninstall from here". 4 hermetic tests cover both an Argo-owned entry not being reported missing and a live Argo-owned release never being an orphan candidate; `kc project test` (post-rebase, re-run by dev:rebase-agent at c19885a) is GREEN.
evidence: post-rebase `kc project test` GREEN at HelmCharts c19885a (dev:rebase-agent run)
